root_idea.summary: The root centers on intrinsic or manifested nobility, excellence, and high worth, especially as moral generosity or honor.
root_idea.development: One semantic branch extends from nobility to generosity, conferring honor, excellent or valuable things, productive land, and divine bounty. A separate branch concerns the necklace and the vine or its clustered grapes.

senses.definition: To honor, dignify, or distinguish someone, including by honoring that person above another.
senses.usage_conditions: The construction with عَلَى expresses preference or elevation above someone else; the broader use denotes the conferral of dignity or special honor.

senses.definition: To honor, treat with courtesy, or confer a beneficent favor upon someone.
senses.usage_conditions: The favor or benefit is understood as one that does not entail humiliation or disgrace; context may render the act as honoring, showing generosity, or making someone comfortable.

senses.definition: Honoring; the conferral of dignity or a noble standing.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic expression ذُو الْجَلَالِ وَالْإِكْرَامِ, the noun can refer to the honoring bestowed by the one described.
In ذُو الْجَلَالِ وَالْإِكْرَامِ, this sense emphasizes universal bounty and gracious beneficence alongside the sense of honoring.

senses.definition: More or most noble, generous, or distinguished.
senses.usage_conditions: The elative form identifies the person or entity highest in the relevant quality; in the Quran this includes moral nobility and supreme generosity.

senses.definition: Possessing or displaying generosity, honor, nobility, excellence, or high worth; noble, honorable, excellent, precious, or distinguished.
senses.usage_conditions: Of a person, the quality is associated with manifested praiseworthy conduct rather than an unexpressed possibility. Of a thing, being كَرِيم means being excellent or distinguished in its own domain, including speech, scripture, produce, place, or status.

senses.definition: Of God, abundantly beneficent and bountiful, showing manifest favor; glorious.
senses.usage_conditions: This specialized divine predication emphasizes generous beneficence and gracious pardon rather than merely human social rank.

senses.definition: Honored, dignified, or treated as worthy of honor.
senses.usage_conditions: This is the passive participle of Form II كَرَّمَ; grammatical gender and number vary with the Quranic noun it describes.

senses.definition: Honored, favored, or accorded a dignified standing.
senses.usage_conditions: This is the passive participle of Form IV أَكْرَمَ and may be substantivized as “the honored ones.”

senses.definition: One who honors, favors, or bestows dignity.
senses.usage_conditions: The active participle denotes the agent who confers honor or gracious treatment.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be or become highly esteemed, excellent, precious, valuable, or rare.
Of land, to become productive or fertile, with good soil and increase of its produce.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a specialized use with land as the subject.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To surpass another in generosity or nobility.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The construction عَلَيْهِ expresses comparison with the person exceeded.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To preserve someone from a thing or keep that thing away from him.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a special use with عَنْ and is distinct from directly honoring someone.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To hold a horse or a similar valuable creature in high regard.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The object is highly esteemed for its quality or worth.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To find a horse generous or excellent in quality.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The construction is used of recognizing the horse's superior quality.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To preserve oneself from a thing or refrain from it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a reflexive protective construction, illustrated with preserving one's honor from an offense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To shun, avoid, or keep oneself far from something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The construction may describe refraining from foul speech or another disapproved matter.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To affect or constrain oneself to be generous.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The use may imply adopting generosity as a deliberate disposition or behavior.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A grape or bunch of grapes.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a lexical expression, not the ordinary adjective كريم.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Generous quality in a horse or similar animal.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The noun denotes the valued or generous quality attributed to the animal.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of land, productive or fertile.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The adjective is used of land that yields good produce.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The precious, excellent, or choice parts of one's possessions, including livestock or other property.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The plural refers to possessions held in especially high estimation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An emphatic refusal: “No, nor anything else.”
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is an idiomatic expression rather than the ordinary noun meaning of honor.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A miracle or thaumaturgical feat attributed to a holy or exceptional person.
Noble or generous, in a positive adjectival use equivalent to كَرِيم rather than a comparative.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This use occurs in expressions describing a person's noble parentage or quality.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An act or occasion of honoring.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This noun is described as a verbal noun related to كَرَّمَ and synonymous with تَكْرِيمٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A means or cause by which honor is attained.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The noun denotes something that leads to honorable standing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A generous or honorable quality, action, practice, or disposition; in the plural, an excellence.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The plural مَكَارِم can refer collectively to noble qualities or deeds.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Good, fertile, well-manured, or well-tilled land producing good herbage or plants.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is the specialized expression أَرْضٌ مَكْرُمَةٌ.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Pointer-only cross-reference for a plant name.
General nobility, generosity, and high worth are covered by the Quranic كريم sense.
The high-bred or excellent horse use is covered by the broader excellence sense.
The valuable or precious thing use is covered by the broader excellence and high-worth sense.
Being held in high estimation is covered by the broader high-worth sense.
The divine glorious-use interpretation is covered by the specialized divine sense.
The related plural expression is covered by the same quality-and-deed meaning.
The plural rendering as excellencies is covered by the same meaning.

cautions: كَرِيم has a broad Quranic excellence branch whose English rendering depends on the referent; divine predication is listed separately because the evidence explicitly gives it the specialized sense of manifest beneficence.
Lane's historical Quran citation notation is not used as a modern verse location; examples use secure QAC locations.
